# Code Review: `vault` package

## Summary
`vault` is a small tenant-scoped file store (`store.go`) fronted by an HTTP server (`server.go`), with a handful of tests (`store_test.go`). No shell tool is available in this environment, so gofmt/vet/tests/lint could not be run — all automated checks are `unavailable (no shell)`. Everything below is from manual reading.

## Findings

### Must Fix

- [ ] **store.go:78** `path()`'s traversal guard is `strings.HasPrefix(p, dir)`, a plain string prefix check, not a path-boundary check. For tenant `"t1"` (`dir = root/t1`) and `name = "../t12/secret.txt"`, `p` cleans to `root/t12/secret.txt`, which still has the string prefix `root/t1` and is wrongly accepted — letting tenant `t1` read/write/delete files under sibling tenant `t12` (or any tenant whose name has `t1` as a prefix).
      Evidence: plausible (traced by hand; `TestPathRejectsEscape` only exercises a non-prefix-colliding sibling name, so it doesn't catch this).
      Fix: compare against `dir` with a separator, e.g. `if p != dir && !strings.HasPrefix(p, dir+string(filepath.Separator)) { return "", ErrBadName }`.

- [ ] **store.go:48** `Meta.ETag()` ranges over `m.Labels`, a Go map, and writes each `k=v` pair into the hash in iteration order. Map iteration order is randomized per run/call, so for any `Meta` with two or more labels, `ETag()` is **not** stable — it can return a different value on successive calls in the same process, breaking the documented guarantee ("comes out the same on every node") and defeating the whole point of the ETag (browser caching, the 304 path in `handleGet`). `TestETagIsStable` only uses a single label, so it can't observe the bug.
      Evidence: plausible (map iteration order is a documented Go language guarantee to be randomized; not independently run here).
      Fix: sort the label keys before hashing, e.g. `for _, k := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(m.Labels)) { h.Write(...) }`.

- [ ] **store.go:172** `Delete` removes the file and deletes it from `s.files[tenant]`, but never decrements `s.used[tenant]`. Every deleted file's bytes stay counted against the tenant's quota forever, so `Used`/`remaining` drift upward until the tenant is permanently locked out of uploads regardless of what's actually on disk.
      Evidence: plausible (traced by hand; `TestDeleteRemovesFile` checks the file is gone but never checks `Used()` afterward, so the gap isn't caught).
      Fix: look up the file's size before removing it and subtract it from `s.used[tenant]` under the lock, e.g. read `s.files[tenant][name].Size` (or `os.Remove`+`Stat` before removal) and do `s.used[tenant] -= size`.

- [ ] **store.go:100-133** `Put` computes `remaining := s.remaining(tenant)` (line 100), then writes the file, then re-acquires the lock only afterward (line 126) to update `s.used`. Two concurrent `Put` calls for the same tenant (different file names) can both read the same `remaining` before either has committed, letting the tenant's total usage exceed `quota` by up to another full upload — the exact invariant the package's doc comment promises ("a per-tenant quota bounds what is kept").
      Evidence: plausible (race traced by hand, not reproduced with `-race`/concurrent test since no shell available).
      Fix: reserve the space under the lock before writing (e.g. track a "reserved" counter, or hold the tenant's quota bookkeeping locked across the whole write with a per-tenant mutex/serialization), releasing/adjusting on failure.

- [ ] **server.go:123-127** The open-redirect guard only checks `strings.HasPrefix(next, "/")`. A `next` value of `//evil.com` (or `/\evil.com`) still starts with `/` and passes, but browsers treat `//evil.com` as a scheme-relative URL and will redirect off-site — an open redirect on the POST-upload flow.
      Evidence: plausible (standard protocol-relative-URL redirect bypass, not executed here).
      Fix: also reject when it starts with `//` (and normalize backslashes), e.g. `if !strings.HasPrefix(next, "/") || strings.HasPrefix(next, "//") { next = "/" }`.

### Should Fix

- [ ] **store.go:72-82** `path()` validates `name` against traversal but never validates `tenant` itself. If `tenant` contains `..` segments (e.g. `"../../etc"`), `dir := filepath.Join(s.root, tenant)` already resolves outside `root`, and the later `HasPrefix(p, dir)` check trivially passes since `p` is built from that same escaped `dir`. The current `Server` happens to be safe because `authorize` only returns tenant values that already exist as values in `s.tokens`, but `Store`'s exported methods (`Put`/`Open`/`Delete`/`List`/`Used`) take `tenant` directly and its doc promises directory isolation — any other caller passing an unvalidated tenant string breaks that promise.
      Evidence: plausible.
      Fix: validate `tenant` the same way `name` is implicitly protected — reject empty, `.`, `..`, and any tenant containing a path separator (e.g. `tenant != filepath.Base(tenant)` or `strings.ContainsAny(tenant, "/\\")`).

- [ ] **server.go:78** `WriteTimeout: 10 * time.Second` applies to the whole response, including `handleGet` streaming a file that can be as large as a tenant's quota (`maxUpload` alone is 256 MiB). A slow client will have its download truncated mid-transfer once 10s elapses from when the server started reading the request, even though nothing is wrong with the request.
      Evidence: plausible.
      Fix: drop the blanket `WriteTimeout` (rely on `ReadHeaderTimeout` + `http.MaxBytesReader` for the actual defenses) or scale it to the response size, and consider per-handler timeouts instead of a server-wide one.

- [ ] **server.go:188-194** `record` calls `s.audit(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), ev)` synchronously from the request-handling goroutine with no deadline at all (`WithoutCancel` strips both cancellation and deadline). A slow or hanging audit hook will block the client's response indefinitely, and there's no bound on how long the handler goroutine/connection is held.
      Evidence: plausible.
      Fix: wrap with a bounded timeout, e.g. `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 5*time.Second); defer cancel()`.

- [ ] **server.go:58-59** `NewServer` stores the caller's `tokens` map by reference (`tokens: tokens`) and reads it later in `authorize` (server.go:178) without any lock. If the caller retains a reference and mutates the map concurrently (e.g. to rotate tokens), that's a data race with the concurrent handler reads, and it's not documented as taking ownership of the map.
      Evidence: plausible.
      Fix: copy the map in `NewServer` (`maps.Clone(tokens)`), or document clearly that the caller must not mutate it after passing it in.

- [ ] **server.go:257-265** `bufPool`/`encode` adds a `sync.Pool` of `*bytes.Buffer` for JSON responses without evidence this is a hot path that needs it; it's extra state and a subtler ownership story (buffer returned to the pool while its bytes are still being written via `w.Write(body)` at line 276 — the pooled buffer is reused/reset by another goroutine potentially before `Write` finishes copying `body`, since `body` aliases the pool buffer's backing array).
      Evidence: plausible — `body := buf.Bytes()` is returned from `encode` while `defer bufPool.Put(buf)` runs at `encode`'s return, before `writeJSON` calls `w.Write(body)`; a concurrent `Get`+`Reset`+reuse of that same buffer during `w.Write` would corrupt `body`. This is a real aliasing bug, not just style.
      Fix: either copy the bytes out before returning them (`slices.Clone(buf.Bytes())`), or write directly into `w` while holding the buffer (`json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)` after setting headers, or keep the buffer local and put it back only after `w.Write` completes).

### Nits

- [ ] **store.go:51** `ETag()` truncates the SHA-256 digest to 32 hex chars (128 bits). Fine for a cache validator, but worth a short comment noting the truncation is intentional rather than a leftover.
- [ ] **server.go:221-229** `clientIP` trusts `X-Forwarded-For` unconditionally for rate-limiting; the doc comment says it's only valid "as the proxy in front of the vault reports it," but nothing in the package enforces that this server actually sits behind such a proxy — worth a startup flag/config to make the trust boundary explicit rather than implicit in a comment.
- [ ] **store_test.go** has no test for `Delete` + `Used()` (would have caught the quota-leak bug) and no multi-label `ETag()` test (would have caught the map-ordering bug) — both gaps line up exactly with the two Must Fix correctness bugs above.

## Automated Checks
`gate: INCOMPLETE — gofmt unavailable (no shell), go vet unavailable (no shell), go build unavailable (no shell), go test -race unavailable (no shell), golangci-lint unavailable (no shell)`

## Not Reviewed
No shell/Bash tool was available in this session, so nothing was compiled, vetted, linted, or run — every finding above is from manual reading only (`plausible`), not `verified`. Recommend running `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./vault/...`, `go test -race ./vault/...`, and `golangci-lint run ./vault/...` before merging.

# Code Review: `partner` package

## Summary
Reviewed `client.go`, `guard.go`, `client_test.go` as a static read (no execution tool available in this session). Solid design (breaker/limiter/backoff, redacted credentials, SSRF guard on `Status`), but several concrete correctness/security bugs.

## Findings

### Must Fix

- [ ] `client.go:98` — `c.log.Debug("submit shipment", "credentials", c.creds, ...)` logs `c.creds` by value, but `String()` (`client.go:43`) has a **pointer** receiver (`func (c *Credentials) String() string`). A `Credentials` value does not satisfy `fmt.Stringer`, so slog falls back to reflecting the struct and prints `Secret` in the clear — defeating the exact protection the doc comment on `Credentials` claims to provide.
      Evidence: plausible (read; `*Credentials` receiver vs. value passed to `Debug`)
      Fix: log `&c.creds` instead of `c.creds` (or change the receiver to a value receiver).

- [ ] `client.go:227-236` — `Label` builds and fetches `strings.TrimSuffix(statusURL, "/status")+"/label"` from a client-supplied `receipt` but never calls `c.partnerURL`, unlike `Status` (`client.go:176`) which validates the host precisely to stop "a tampered receipt [pointing] the shop at an internal address." A forged/tampered receipt makes `Label` an SSRF primitive that `Status` explicitly closed.
      Evidence: plausible (read)
      Fix: validate the derived URL with `c.partnerURL` before issuing the request, same as `Status`.

- [ ] `client.go:108,110` — `payload := bytes.NewReader(body)` is created once before the retry loop and reused across attempts (`req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, ..., payload)` inside the `for attempt := range c.attempts` loop). After the first attempt is actually sent, the reader is drained to EOF; every retried attempt therefore submits an **empty body** to the partner.
      Evidence: plausible (read; `bytes.Reader` is not reset/recreated between iterations)
      Fix: create a fresh `bytes.NewReader(body)` per attempt (inside the loop), or `payload.Seek(0, io.SeekStart)` before each retry.

- [ ] `client.go:209-210` — `Wait`'s `for {}` loop calls `context.WithTimeout(ctx, interval)` and `defer cancel()` on every iteration. Since the loop only exits via `return`, every poll's timer/context leaks until `Wait` itself returns — for a long-running wait this accumulates one live timer per tick.
      Evidence: plausible (read; classic defer-in-loop leak)
      Fix: call `cancel()` explicitly at the end of each iteration (or via an inner function) instead of deferring inside the loop.

- [ ] `client.go:294` — `retryAfter` returns `time.Duration(secs)` where `secs` is a count of **seconds** parsed from the `Retry-After` header, but `time.Duration` is a count of **nanoseconds**. A `Retry-After: 5` becomes 5ns, not 5s, so the computed backoff (`wait = max(wait, pe.retryAfter)` at `client.go:135`) never actually honors the partner's requested pause.
      Evidence: plausible (read)
      Fix: `return time.Duration(secs) * time.Second`.

- [ ] `client.go:301` vs `client.go:306` — `EncodeReceipt` encodes with `base64.RawURLEncoding` (unpadded), but `DecodeReceipt` decodes with `base64.URLEncoding` (expects `=` padding). Any receipt whose raw length isn't a multiple of 4 fails to decode with `illegal base64 data` even though it was produced by this package's own encoder.
      Evidence: plausible (read; encoding/decoding mismatch)
      Fix: decode with `base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString` to match the encoder.

- [ ] `client.go:227,246-249,254` — `Label` has no named return value, yet the deferred flush handler does `if ferr := bw.Flush(); ferr != nil && err == nil { err = ferr }` and the function ends with `return err`. Because the return isn't named, `return err` evaluates and stores the return value *before* the deferred closure runs; the closure's mutation of the local `err` variable happens too late to affect what the caller receives. A `Flush` failure (truncated label on disk) is silently swallowed, contradicting "the label is complete when Label returns nil."
      Evidence: plausible (read; unnamed return + defer-mutates-local pattern)
      Fix: give `Label` a named return (`) (err error) {`) so the deferred assignment actually propagates, or restructure to check `bw.Flush()` explicitly after `io.Copy` instead of in a `defer`.

### Should Fix

- [ ] `guard.go:29-31` — `Allow` computes whole `int(now.Sub(l.last).Seconds())*l.rate` tokens, then unconditionally sets `l.last = now`, discarding the sub-second remainder every call. Under frequent calls (sub-second intervals) the bucket refills slower than `rate` actually allows because the leftover fraction is thrown away each time rather than carried forward.
      Evidence: plausible (read)
      Fix: track elapsed time with a duration-based accumulator (e.g. keep fractional nanoseconds, or use `float64` tokens) instead of truncating to whole seconds each call.

- [ ] `guard.go:59-65` — Once the cooldown has elapsed, `Allow()` returns `true` for *every* concurrent caller (there's no "probe in flight" flag), so multiple goroutines can all send a probe request simultaneously instead of the single probe the doc comment ("lets one probe through per cooldown") promises.
      Evidence: plausible (read)
      Fix: consume a one-shot half-open token inside `Allow` (e.g. reset `openedAt` past the cooldown window, or add an explicit `probing bool` guarded by the mutex) so only one caller gets `true` per cooldown.

- [ ] `client.go:214` — `st.State == "delivered"` is a bare magic string duplicating the partner's wire vocabulary with no shared constant; a typo or a future rename of the partner's state strings won't be caught by the compiler.
      Evidence: plausible (read)
      Fix: define a named constant (e.g. `const StateDelivered = "delivered"`) alongside `Status` and use it here.

### Nits

- [ ] `client.go:144` — `try` (unexported) sits between the exported `Submit` and `Status` methods, and `EncodeReceipt`/`DecodeReceipt` (exported utilities, `client.go:300-315`) sit after the unexported `backoff`/`pause`/`retryAfter` helpers, both against the checklist's types→constructors→exported→unexported→utilities ordering.
- [ ] `client.go:75-90` — `attempts`, `maxWait`, limiter `(20, 40)`, and breaker `(5, 30s)` are hardcoded in `New` with no way for a caller to override them; worth a second thought if different partner accounts ever need different limits.

## Automated Checks
`gate: INCOMPLETE — no shell/execution tool available in this session; gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint, and `go test` were not run. All findings above are from static reading only.`

## Not Reviewed
- Whether `client_test.go` covers the bugs found (it doesn't exercise a retry that would hit the drained-body bug, the `Label` SSRF path, or the `Retry-After` unit bug) — worth adding regression tests once fixes land.
- Runtime verification (build/vet/test/race) — needs a shell tool or CI run.

# Code Review: `orders` package

## Summary
Two files: `server.go` (HTTP handlers) and `store.go` (SQL-backed store). No diff was supplied, so the whole package was reviewed as non-test code, security/DB/HTTP first per risk order.

## Findings

### Must Fix
- **store.go:46** SQL injection: `customer` is spliced into the query with `fmt.Sprintf` instead of a placeholder, even though the same function already uses `$1` elsewhere in the file.
  Evidence: plausible (read)
  Fix: `query += " WHERE customer = $1"` and pass `customer` as a `QueryContext` argument (build the args slice conditionally).

- **store.go:76** The `order_events` insert runs on `s.db` instead of `tx`, so it is not part of the transaction started at line 65. A failure here does not roll back the order insert, and the event row can become visible before (or independent of) the order's commit, breaking the atomicity the transaction is supposed to provide.
  Evidence: plausible (read)
  Fix: change to `tx.ExecContext(ctx, ...)`.

- **server.go:39** `handleGet` calls `s.store.Get(context.Background(), id)` instead of `r.Context()`, unlike `handleList`/`handleCreate` which correctly use the request context. This drops client-cancellation/timeout propagation for this endpoint.
  Evidence: plausible (read)
  Fix: use `r.Context()`.

- **server.go:63** Logs the raw `Authorization` header at Info level on every create request. This puts bearer tokens/credentials into logs.
  Evidence: plausible (read)
  Fix: remove the header from the log line entirely (or log only whether it was present, never the value).

- **server.go:79** `go s.store.Audit(r.Context(), id)` starts a goroutine using the request context after the handler is about to return a response. Once `ServeHTTP` returns, `net/http` cancels the request context, so this audit call races the response write and will typically be canceled before or during the query, silently failing. The returned error is also discarded, so failures are invisible.
  Evidence: plausible (read)
  Fix: use a decoupled context, e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(r.Context())` (or `context.Background()` with an explicit timeout), and log the error if `Audit` fails: `if err := s.store.Audit(ctx, id); err != nil { s.log.Error(...) }`.

- **server.go:46** On any non-`ErrNotFound` failure, `handleGet` returns `err.Error()` directly to the client (`http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)`), leaking internal error/database detail, while `handleList`/`handleCreate` correctly return a generic "internal error" message.
  Evidence: verified (read/compared against sibling handlers in the same file)
  Fix: log `err` via `s.log.Error` and respond with a generic message, matching the other handlers.

- **server.go:30** `ListenAndServe` calls the bare `http.ListenAndServe`, which has no header/read/write timeouts (Slowloris exposure) and no graceful shutdown hook.
  Evidence: plausible (read)
  Fix: construct `&http.Server{Addr: addr, Handler: s.mux, ReadHeaderTimeout: ...}` and call its `ListenAndServe`.

### Should Fix
- **server.go:79** The lifetime of the audit goroutine is undocumented and unbounded — every `POST /orders` spawns one with no cap, backpressure, or way to know it finished. If load requires async auditing, use a bounded worker pool or a queue; otherwise call `Audit` synchronously before responding.
  Evidence: plausible (read)
  Fix: either await `Audit` before responding, or add a documented, bounded async mechanism.

### Nits
- **store.go:52** `orders := []Order{}` produces a non-nil empty slice; if the `[]` vs `null` JSON distinction for an empty search result is intentional for API stability, worth a one-line comment noting why (`go-data-structures` otherwise recommends `var orders []Order`).

## Automated Checks
`gate: INCOMPLETE` — no shell/bash tool available in this session, so `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go build`, `go test -race`, and `golangci-lint` were not run. Findings are from manual reading only (`plausible` unless noted `verified`).

## Not Reviewed
No test files exist for this package (`orders_test.go` etc. not found), so test quality/coverage was not assessed — flagging that no tests exist for the SQL-injection and transaction bugs above is itself worth raising with the author separately.

## Review: `books` package

**Automated checks:** unavailable — no shell/bash tool in this environment, so `gofmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint`, and `go fix -diff` were not run. Everything below is from manual reading.

---

### Must Fix

- **store.go:73** (verified) — `Entries` scans columns in the wrong order. The query selects `debit_cents, credit_cents` (store.go:14) but `rows.Scan` fills `&e.Credit, &e.Debit` — debit and credit are swapped for every entry returned by this method. Contrast with `Entry` (singular) at store.go:47, which scans `&e.Debit, &e.Credit` correctly for the same column order. **Fix:** `rows.Scan(&e.ID, &e.AccountID, &e.Debit, &e.Credit, &e.Memo, &e.PostedAt)`.

- **store.go:16** (verified) — `entriesQuery` uses `id >= $2`, but the `Entries` doc comment (store.go:58) promises entries "posted after the entry with id `after`" (exclusive). A caller paginating with `after` = last id of the previous page will get that same entry again as the first row of the next page. **Fix:** `id > $2`.

- **store.go:47** (verified) — `Entry` scans the `memo` column directly into `e.Memo string` with no `COALESCE`, unlike `Entries` (store.go:14) which explicitly wraps it in `COALESCE(memo, '')`. If `memo` is NULL (which the other query treats as a real possibility), `Scan` returns an error ("unsupported Scan… converting NULL to string"). **Fix:** either wrap in `COALESCE(memo, '')` in the query or scan into a `sql.NullString` and set `e.Memo` from it.

- **store.go:113-121** (verified) — `Transfer` locks the `from` account with `FOR UPDATE` (line 103) but reads the `to` account's balance with a plain, unlocked `SELECT` (line 114) and then writes it back as an absolute value (`SET balance_cents = $1`, line 121) instead of `balance_cents = balance_cents + $1`. Two concurrent transfers crediting the same `to` account can both read the same `toBalance`, and the second commit clobbers the first — a lost update / balance corruption bug. **Fix:** make the credit atomic like the debit: `UPDATE accounts SET balance_cents = balance_cents + $1 WHERE id = $2`, and drop the separate read of `toBalance` (or lock it with `FOR UPDATE` if the row still needs reading for other reasons).

- **books.go:94-101** (verified) — `ParseAccountIDs` doc says "An empty list is valid and selects every account," but `strings.Split("", ",")` returns `[""]`, and `strconv.ParseInt("", 10, 64)` fails, so `ParseAccountIDs("")` returns an error instead of `nil, nil`. **Fix:** special-case the empty/blank input, e.g. `if strings.TrimSpace(s) == "" { return nil, nil }` before splitting.

- **books.go:130** (verified) — `NextBillingDate`'s doc promises "the same day of the following month, or that month's last day when it is shorter," but the implementation is a bare `t.AddDate(0, 1, 0)`. Go's `AddDate` overflows on day rollover (e.g. Jan 31 + 1 month becomes Mar 3, not Feb 28), so the documented "clamp to last day" behavior is not implemented. **Fix:** compute the following month's day count and clamp, e.g. construct the first of the next-next month and step back a day when the naive `AddDate` result's month has skipped.

- **books.go:136** (verified) — `StartOfDay` does `t.In(loc).Truncate(24 * time.Hour)`. `time.Time.Truncate` operates on the absolute duration since the Go zero time, not on the wall-clock/local presentation, so for any location whose UTC offset isn't a whole multiple that aligns with the epoch (e.g. UTC+5:30, UTC+5:45, and some DST transitions) this does not return local midnight. The existing test only checks `time.UTC`, so it doesn't catch this. **Fix:** `y, m, d := t.In(loc).Date(); return time.Date(y, m, d, 0, 0, 0, 0, loc)`.

- **books.go:35** (verified) — `Account.Equal` omits `Frozen` from the comparison even though `Frozen` is a field of `Account` and the doc says it decides "whether a row changed since the last sync." A frozen/unfrozen transition would be silently treated as "no change." **Fix:** add `&& a.Frozen == b.Frozen`.

- **books.go:68-71** (verified) — `Statement.Clone` clones `Entries` but not `Totals` (a `map[string]int64`). Maps are reference types, so the clone still shares the original's map; per the doc, the renderer "sorts and annotates" the clone "without touching the statement the store handed out," but writes to `Totals` on the clone will mutate the original too. **Fix:** clone the map as well, e.g. `s.Totals = maps.Clone(s.Totals)`.

### Should Fix

- **books.go:87-89** (plausible) — `Fee`'s doc states a refund "carries a negative fee of the same magnitude as the fee on the charge it reverses," but `(amount*bps + 5_000) / 10_000` truncates toward zero, so `Fee(30, 250) == 1` while `Fee(-30, 250) == 0` — not symmetric. This is even called out in the test name "small refund carries no fee" (books_test.go:17), which directly contradicts the doc comment. Either fix the doc to describe the true (asymmetric) rounding, or fix the formula to round symmetrically (e.g. round by sign of `amount`) if the doc is the intended contract.

- **store.go:92-136** (plausible) — `Transfer` never checks `from != to`. A self-transfer locks the same row twice (harmless in Postgres within one session) but then performs `balance -= amount` followed by `balance = toBalance + amount` where `toBalance` was read before either update — net effect is the balance increases by `amount` instead of staying flat, fabricating money. **Fix:** reject `from == to` up front.

- **store.go:103, 118-121** (plausible) — Lock ordering: `from` is locked with `FOR UPDATE` first, then `to` is updated (which itself takes a row lock in Postgres). Two concurrent transfers in opposite directions (A→B and B→A) can deadlock, since each transaction acquires its first lock in a different order. **Fix:** always lock the two accounts in a fixed order (e.g. by id) regardless of transfer direction.

- **books_test.go:28-36** (verified) — `TestParseAccountIDs` only covers the success path; it doesn't test the empty-string case ("selects every account" per the doc) or a malformed id, which is exactly the case that's broken (see Must Fix above). Add cases for `""` and an invalid id.

- **books_test.go:50-55** (verified) — `TestNextBillingDate` only exercises a mid-month date; it doesn't test a month-end date (e.g. Jan 31), which is the case the doc explicitly calls out and which is currently broken. Add that case.

- **books_test.go:57-63** (verified) — `TestStartOfDay` only exercises `time.UTC`; add a non-whole-hour-offset location (e.g. `Asia/Kolkata`, UTC+5:30) to catch the `Truncate` bug above.

### Nit

- **store.go:88-89** (plausible) — `Transfer`'s doc says "Accounts of one customer share a currency, so none is checked," but nothing in the function actually establishes that `from` and `to` belong to the same customer — this is an unstated caller obligation. Worth a one-line comment on the precondition or a defensive check if callers can't be trusted to hold it.

# Code Review: invoice package

## Summary
Single-file package (`invoice/invoice.go`, 103 lines) implementing an `Invoice`/`Line` model and a `TextRenderer`. No test file exists in the package. No automated tooling (gofmt/vet/lint) was run — no shell tool is available in this session, so all findings below are `plausible` (read-only review), not `verified`.

## Findings

### Must Fix
- [ ] [invoice.go:81-83] `formatCents` mis-renders negative amounts. Since `Line` docs explicitly allow "a negative UnitCents is a credit," a negative total or negative line amount is a supported case, but `c/100` and `c%100` on a negative `c` produce a negative fraction (e.g. `c = -150` → `"$-1.-50"` instead of `"-$1.50"`).

  Evidence: plausible (net/http `*bytes.Reader` handling in `http.NewRequest`).
  Fix: build a fresh reader per attempt, e.g. `bytes.NewReader(body)` inside the `for attempt := range c.attempts` loop.

A flush failure after a successful `io.Copy` is silently swallowed and `Label` reports success with a truncated/unflushed label.
  Evidence: plausible (Go semantics: defer only affects already-returned unnamed values through a named result parameter).

Those already-running goroutines will block forever on `errs <- job(p.ctx)` once their job returns, since nothing reads from `errs` after the early return. Every partial run leaks one goroutine per in-flight job. Fix: use a buffered/drained channel, a `sync.WaitGroup`, or select on both `errs` and `ctx.Done()` in the collection loop so in-flight goroutines are always drained.

Any concurrent call to `Failed`/`Snapshot` while `Run` is in progress (or two concurrent `Run` calls on the same `*Pool`) is a data race on `p.failed`. Fix: hold `p.mu` around every read/write of `p.failed`, including inside `Run`.

- **pool.go:74-80** (verified) — `Once` calls `fn(ctx)` at line 80 while still holding `p.mu` (locked at 74, deferred unlock at 75). This serializes every `Once`-wrapped job across the entire pool — defeating the purpose of a bounded concurrent worker pool — and risks a deadlock if `fn` ever calls back into any other `Pool` method that also takes `p.mu` (e.g. `Failed`, `Snapshot`, or another `Once`).       Evidence: plausible (read)
      Fix: `return time.Duration(secs) * time.Second`.

- [ ] `client.go:108,110` The same `*bytes.Reader` (`payload`) is reused across every retry attempt in `Submit`'s loop. After the first attempt's body is sent, the reader is at EOF; every retried attempt therefore sends an empty request body, silently corrupting the retried submission.
      Evidence: plausible (read)

Fix: copy the bytes out before returning, or keep the buffer held until after the write completes, e.g. write directly into `w` inside a helper that pools the buffer around the whole `w.Write` call rather than returning its backing slice. (verified — sync.Pool + returned-alias-slice race)

**server.go:123-129 (`handlePut`)** — the open-redirect guard `if !strings.HasPrefix(next, "/") { next = "/" }` accepts `next=//evil.com/...`, which starts with `/` but browsers treat as a protocol-relative URL to an external host — an open redirect after a successful POST upload. Fix: also reject a second leading `/` (or parse with `url.Parse` and require an empty `Host`):
```go
if !strings.HasPrefix(next, "/") || strings.HasPrefix(next, "//") {
    next = "/"
}
```
(verified)

## Should Fix

**server.go:221-229 (`clientIP`)** — `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted unconditionally with no check that the request actually came through a trusted proxy. Any client can set this header to spoof its rate-limit identity, either evading `allowUpload`'s per-address cap entirely (new fake address every request) or flooding another tenant's bucket. Combined with server.go:237-243, spoofed fresh addresses also prevent the `hits` map from ever being pruned (only entries older than a minute are deleted), so this also enables unbounded memory growth. Fix: only trust `X-Forwarded-For` when the immediate peer is a known/trusted proxy, or use `r.RemoteAddr` directly if the vault is expected to be reachable directly.

**server.go:74-79 (`ListenAndServe`)** — `WriteTimeout: 10 * time.Second` on an `http.Server` that accepts uploads up to `maxUpload` (256 MiB, server.go:20) is very tight: per `net/http` docs, `WriteTimeout` starts counting from when headers are read and covers the time spent reading the request body in the handler, so a legitimate but modest-bandwidth client (well under 25.6 MB/s) will have its upload cut off mid-transfer. Fix: raise `WriteTimeout` (or drop it and rely on `ReadHeaderTimeout` plus a context deadline) to something proportional to `maxUpload`.

**store.go:56-193 (file ordering)** — the unexported helpers `path` (store.go:72) and `remaining` (store.go:85) are placed before the exported methods `Put`, `Open`, `Delete`, `List`, `Used`, contrary to the house convention (types → constructors → exported methods → unexported → utilities). **server.go:133-157 / store.go (Content-Type echo)** — `Content-Type` is taken verbatim from the uploader's header (server.go:117) and echoed back unchanged when another caller fetches the file (server.go:151), with no allow-list and no `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. If the vault is ever served from an origin that shares cookies/session with a browser app, an uploader can set `Content-Type: text/html` and get stored content rendered as HTML for anyone who opens the file URL. Fix: add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and/or restrict `Content-Type` to a safe allow-list (or force `Content-Disposition: attachment`) unless the deployment guarantees an isolated origin for served files.
